title: Ramanuja's Commentary on the Bhagavad Gita
dateDisplay: c. first half of the 12th century CE
author: ramanuja
attributionNote: Commentary by Ramanuja on all eighteen chapters of the Bhagavad Gita, written from the standpoint of Vishishtadvaita and drawing on the older commentary attributed to Yamuna.
description: Ramanuja reads the Gita as a single argument: that action performed as worship, knowable through knowledge of the self as a mode of Brahman, leads to the vision of the Lord, and that devotion to the Lord is both the means and the goal. Each verse is printed with his prose commentary on it, chapter by chapter and verse by verse.
historicalContext: The Gita Bhashya is the Gita commentary of the Shri Vaishnava tradition and one of the three most influential readings of the poem, standing beside Shankara's Advaita commentary and Madhva's Dvaita commentary.
availabilityNote: Complete: the Sanskrit verses of the Gita with Ramanuja's commentary on them, streamed from GRETIL at read time, one chapter at a time. This is the original Sanskrit, not a translation, and the commentary is printed with the verse it explains.
